Following are radio stations in the [[United States of America]] affiliated with colleges and universities that are regarded as [[Campus radio|college (student-run)]] stations. The listings include links to Wikipedia pages on the [[Radio broadcasting|stations]], their parent institutions, and their cities and states of license.

Separate lists are included to differentiate between stations that are [[license]]d by the [[Federal Communications Commission]] (FCC) and those that [[Broadcasting|broadcast]] solely by way of the [[Internet radio|internet]]:

Two broad categories apply to licensed stations owned by U.S. colleges and universities:
* [[Campus radio|Student-run]] — Stations where students play significant roles in programming, management, and other facets of operations, either on their own, through student government organizations, or under faculty supervision. Many student-run stations also allow [[Community radio|community volunteers]] to participate as [[Disc jockey|program hosts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://radio-locator.com/cgi-bin/format?code=col |title=College Radio Stations |website=radio-locator.com |publisher=Radio-Locator |access-date=November 6, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.radiosurvivor.com/learn-more/about-college-radio/ |title=About College Radio |date=March 14, 2023 |website=radiosurvivor.com |publisher=Radio Survivor |access-date=November 10, 2024}}</ref>
* [[Public radio|Public broadcasting]] — Stations operated either by their parent institutions or in partnership with public broadcasting organizations in the communities or regions they serve.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/features/article/10018-does-college-radio-even-matter-anymore/ |title=Does College Radio Even Matter Anymore? |last=Lozano |first=Kevin |date=February 8, 2017 |website=pitchfork.com |publisher=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|access-date=November 10, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Shapiro |first=Ari |author-link=Ari Shapiro |editor1-last=Roberts |editor1-first=Cokie |editor1-link=Cokie Roberts |editor2-last=Stamberg |editor2-first=Susan |editor2-link=Susan Stamberg |title=This Is NPR |page=228 |publisher=Chronicle Books |year=2010 |location=San Francisco |url=https://archive.org/details/thisisnpr00robe/mode/2up |isbn=9780811872539 |ref=}}</ref> According to their websites, these stations operate as public radio stations with little if any student programming. Therefore, they are not included in the listing.
